title: Who influenced her and whether anyone imitated her
summary: She says nobody identified her style with anyone, citing Adelaide Hall and wordless vocals with Ellington.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well I don't think that they knew what was happening at the time. Nobody does the things that I -- nobody sing them. I've heard orchestrations, and I've heard male singers do it -- do like some of the things that I'm doing now on my current repertoire. But of the females, I don't hear them doing any of the things that I do. Of course, I attended the first performance of 'Black Broadway,' and Adelaide was doing some of things I do. But Adelaide did them before I was doing them. So, if anything, I was emulating Adelaide

Hall, which, perhaps -- Well, I mean, I would -- I was influenced by her material. But I think because Adelaide was not in the United States, and nobody at the time, you know, knew about Adelaide, she wasn't among the current scheme of pop singers.
Yeah. And mostly she was known for doing the wordless vocal with Duke Ellington.

That's right. So, I don't think that anybody identified my renditions with Adelaide. And then, of course, Adelaide's style and my style are entirely different. So I would not be imitating Adelaide. I would just be singing some of the songs that she made famous. And then, of course, I had listened to Adelaide Hall in my younger days before I ever thought about coming to New York or becoming popular. I had heard Adelaide, in fact, in Pittsburgh.
